status: MEASURED OFFLINE; native ids handled only as counts

evidence_labels.MEASURED: counted or timed from a recorded run or committed evidence file
evidence_labels.VERIFIED: read directly from code, config or a file's contents
evidence_labels.INFERRED: a model with its assumptions stated beside it
evidence_labels.UNKNOWN: the evidence does not exist; not the same as zero

code.label: VERIFIED
code.job_key: req_number if present -> ('req', req); else normalized company (corporate suffixes stripped) + order-insensitive title -> ('ct', c, t); else host+path of the URL -> ('url', u); else None (never deduped)
code.dedupe: rank_rows: stable sort by score descending, then the first row per job_key survives; unkeyed rows all survive
code.survivor: highest score; on a tie, arrival order: paid rows first in plan order, then free in registry order (lever, greenhouse, ashby, smartrecruiters, breezy, feeds); concurrency keeps registry order
code.cross_provider: the same job_key across providers is one posting — the only cross-provider identity the engine has
code.native_capture: sources/ats.py and sources/feeds.py stash '_native' ONLY while telemetry is active; paid rows (linkedin, indeed) get none
code.exports: to_output() never reads '_native' (asserted in scraper's self-check); CSV/JSON carry apply_url, in which most ATS ids are visible
code.namespace_precedent: sources/shadow.py already compares (provider family, native_id), never the raw id alone
code.seen_ledger: seen.tsv lines are date<TAB>'|'.join(job_key)<TAB>title<TAB>company, appended by record_seen from OUTPUT rows; read by --only-new, which the worker never passes
code.other_ledgers: sweep applied.tsv and the live feed key on scraper._seen_key of output rows; .done_combos keys search combos (date|site|keyword|location), not postings

c5_final_url_ids.label: MEASURED (201 exported rows; id parsed from apply_url)

c5_within_sweep.label: MEASURED; distinct ids inside one board INFERRED except the eight shadow boards, where C5 VERIFIED native_id_distinct == gated

concept.definition: native_identity = (provider family, native id) inside one provider, job_key when the id is missing or malformed, cross-provider identity unchanged

split_effect_in_c5.label: MEASURED upper bound at the gate; final effect UNKNOWN
split_effect_in_c5.meaning: rows the current key merges inside one board although each has its own id (mostly one title posted in several locations): native-first identity would show them separately — the opposite of job_key's deliberate 'not on location' rule, and a product decision

merge_effect_in_c5.label: MEASURED
merge_effect_in_c5.meaning: within one sweep a board lists an id once, so a merge-only rule changes nothing

merge_effect_across_time.label: MEASURED
merge_effect_across_time.who_benefits: seen.tsv (--only-new, CLI only) and applied.tsv (local sweep UI); nothing on the public worker path

migration.label: VERIFIED (code) + MEASURED (ledgers)
migration.seen_tsv: old entries stay meaningful: every well-formed 'ct' entry recomputes to its stored key under current job_key; a native key would have to be ADDED beside it (dual lookup), never replace it
migration.historical_outputs: carry no native id; apply_url yields one for greenhouse, lever, ashby, smartrecruiters, linkedin and indeed rows only
migration.done_combos: untouched by any identity change (keys search combos)
migration.blocker: native ids exist only when telemetry is on, so dedupe on them would make results depend on a diagnostics flag until capture is unconditional

why: C5 would have merged 0 more rows (same id under two keys: 0 in the final set and 0 between shadow and production)
native-first identity would instead SPLIT up to 718 gated rows C5 merged, reversing the deliberate multi-location collapse
the real drift is across time (29 of 1912 recurring ids in history, 19 of 857 in two days on the shadow boards), and only CLI/local ledgers that the public worker never reads would gain
capture is telemetry-gated and paid rows carry no native id
decision.revisit_when: a user-facing ledger (applied, dismissed, new-since-last) ships on the worker path; then add a merge-only dual lookup keyed (family, id) beside job_key, with unconditional capture
